title: Additional residential unit zoning and OLG funding changes
subtitle: Termite program contractor removal, Guelph Owen Sound bus agreement, and a one-year housing reserve allocation.
overview: Council adopted a zoning by-law amendment to regulate additional residential units, bringing local rules in line with provincial requirements. Staff said the changes remove many rules that caused people to need variances, and a public guide is planned to help homeowners through the process.

Council also changed the Ontario Lottery and Gaming (OLG) funding allocation policy. The 2% heritage share will go to a housing reserve for 2026 as seed money for housing work, and the policy will be reviewed as part of the 2027 budget. In the annual termite report, Council removed one contractor from the preferred list and asked that the OLG allocation policy and 2026 budget direction reflect the report's financial analysis.

Council approved an amending agreement with the City of Owen Sound to keep the Guelph Owen Sound Transportation service running in the township. Residents were also told that an update on the Bissell Park ice pad is expected at the December 2 budget meeting. A closed session held earlier had nothing to report.

decisions.detail: Council adopted a zoning by-law amendment regulating additional residential units and confirmed no further public notice is required {{vote:m5}}.
Council directed staff to move the 2% heritage share of OLG funding to the housing reserve for 2026 {{vote:m7}}.
Council authorized a by-law amending the OLG policy as amended, to be used in the 2026 budget and reviewed as part of the 2027 budget {{vote:m8}}.

Council received the report, removed Aetna Pest Control as a preferred Sentricon contractor, and asked that the OLG policy and 2026 budget direction reflect the report's financial analysis {{vote:m6}}.
Council authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the licensing amending agreement with the City of Owen Sound for the bus service in the township {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved the consent items, including the 2026 budget survey results and an appointment to the Wellington County Joint Accessibility Advisory Committee {{vote:m3}}.

debate: On additional residential units, one councillor relayed resident concerns about privacy and the effect of backyard units. Staff replied that provincial policy requires municipalities to facilitate these units and that infrastructure can handle them. Staff added that a three-unit conversion may need a water service review at the building permit stage, at the owner's cost.

On the Guelph Owen Sound bus, councillors asked how the township promotes the $5 fare. Staff suggested working with the communications office and the community profile, and said the transit feasibility study is looking at integration with the service.

On the termite program, councillors said awareness is low and uptake is modest. They urged staff to press the contractors to promote it, rather than leaving it to them, and asked for an updated map of treated zones. Staff said the contractors were expected to lead marketing but agreed to look at the map.

On OLG funding, one councillor proposed redirecting the heritage share to housing seed money. Staff said the heritage reserve could cover 2026 spending but that a longer-term shortfall was possible. Another councillor wanted to hear from heritage representatives first and asked why staff had not proposed housing funding earlier. Staff said economic development also faces pressure from debt on business park land and a contribution to the operations centre.
